theme: Primary object witnesses and bounded extension ledger for readable seal controls
question: Can bounded primary and institutional source recovery add eligible Akkadian and Tamil-Brahmi seal legends to the frozen head-direction comparison?
outcome: Adjudicated 18 candidates with zero new eligible distinct legends: two confirmed duplicates, eleven probable revised-edition duplicates, one deferred seal, two language exclusions and two damaged-edge exclusions. Recovered physical witnesses behind two existing Urkesh legends and restored a 57-page institutional Tamil preview with a specific absent-catalogue target. Original counts remain 11 Akkadian sign-level legends and 23 Tamil-Brahmi including coins, 16 seals and rings.
challenge: The current CICT URL returns 404; the held institutional file is a preview omitting catalogue pp.67 and 70. Akkadian-name royal legend A14.239 has a Hurrian title; other source candidates repeat existing dies or have damaged edges. Seven search queries exceeded the declared six-query bound by one.
remedy: Preserved source hashes, failures, actual displayed page exposure, explicit null fields, physical-object joins, language exclusions and a versioned local-only ledger. Existing corpus files and statistical rules remain unchanged.
retry_when: Acquire revised Tamil catalogue pp.67–70 and its seal and ring plates, or a primary Tell Brak corpus with complete Akkadian legends and physical carrier identifiers; count only new distinct legends after aliases and die joins. A separately declared Old Assyrian period extension may be evaluated without changing the existing Sargonic cohort.
